title: Connected special fibre of a quasi-reductive model over a DVR
statement:
Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], with fraction field $K$, residue field $k$, and an algebraic closure $\bar k$ of $k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $\mathcal G=\operatorname{Spec}B$ be affine over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], where $B$ is a finitely generated flat $A$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Suppose $\mathcal G$ is equipped with multiplication $\mathcal G\times_A\mathcal G\to\mathcal G$, an identity $\operatorname{Spec}A\to\mathcal G$, and an inverse, satisfying the group diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme] with base $\operatorname{Spec}A$; the fibre product is [def-pc-fibre-product]. Assume its generic fibre $\mathcal G_K$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and geometrically connected, meaning connected after every field extension of $K$. Let $H$ be the connected component containing the identity in the reduced scheme underlying $\mathcal G_{\bar k}$. Suppose $H$, with its induced group law, is reductive: smooth, connected, affine of finite type, with no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent closed subgroup; unipotent means unipotent matrices in a faithful linear representation. Assume
$$\dim H=\dim\mathcal G_K,$$
where dimension is Krull dimension of the underlying scheme. Then $\mathcal G_{\bar k}$ is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme]. There is no restriction on the residue characteristic and no smoothness hypothesis on $\mathcal G$ over $A$.

source.place: WANTED locally: G. Prasad and J.-K. Yu, On quasi-reductive group schemes, Theorem 1.2(c), printed pp.1-2; finite-type proof in Proposition 4.4(i) and the first paragraph of Section 5, printed pp.8-9. Read online at https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0405381. Geometric form obtained by the local extension of DVRs used at the start of Section 5. Milne iAG (2017), printed p.509, cites Prasad-Yu (2006).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-group-model-potential-smooth-normalization] to the given affine flat finite-type group. Obtain $A\to R$ with residue field the specified $\bar k$, a smooth affine model $\mathcal N$, and a finite surjective special-fibre homomorphism $q:\mathcal N_{\bar k}\to\mathcal G_{\bar k}$. Its generic fibre is $\mathcal G_K\times_K L$, hence geometrically connected by the hypothesis on $\mathcal G_K$. The target special fibre is literally the one in the conclusion, since the residue embedding was fixed.

source.place: Proposition 3.4, Corollary A.4 and the local-extension reduction in Section 5

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-group-cover-reductive-neutral] to $q$ over the algebraically closed field $\bar k$. Its source is smooth and its target has reduced neutral component $H$, reductive by hypothesis. It follows that $(\mathcal N_{\bar k})^0$ is reductive. This application permits inseparable finite kernels, including in characteristic $2$.

source.place: Proposition 4.3 first paragraph, finite normalization case in Proposition 4.4(i)

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-model-reductive-neutral-lift] over the henselian ring $R$. The preceding step verifies the special-fibre hypothesis and Step 1 verifies geometric connectedness of the generic fibre. Obtain a split reductive open affine subgroup $\mathcal D\subseteq\mathcal N$ with $\mathcal D_L=\mathcal N_L$ and $\mathcal D_{\bar k}=(\mathcal N_{\bar k})^0$.

Let $E=R[\mathcal N]$. By its integral-closure construction in Step 1, $E=C$ is a subring of its generic coordinate algebra $E[1/\pi]=L[\mathcal N_L]$; generic restriction identifies $\mathcal N(R)$ with a subgroup $M\subseteq\mathcal N_L(L)$. Indeed, maps $E\to R$ agreeing in $L$ agree in $R$. For each $f\in E[1/\pi]$, write $f=\pi^{-a}e$ with $e\in E$ and $a\geq0$. Every $x\in M$ satisfies $e(x)\in R$, so $v(f(x))\geq-a$. Thus $M$ is bounded in precisely the sense of [lem-sfb-split-reductive-integral-maximal-bounded]. The inclusion $\mathcal D\subseteq\mathcal N$ gives $\mathcal D(R)\subseteq M$, and that lemma yields $M=\mathcal D(R)$.

source.place: Lemma 3.7 and Proposition 4.3 second paragraph; coordinate argument for boundedness

proof.text: Every $\bar k$-point of $\mathcal N_{\bar k}$ lifts to an $R$-point of $\mathcal N$: since $\mathcal N=\operatorname{Spec}E$ is smooth, [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine] says $E$ is a smooth $R$-algebra, and [lem-trf-henselian-smooth-algebra-lifting] with base ring $R$, target algebra $R$, and ideal its maximal ideal lifts any map $E\to\bar k$ to $E\to R$. The pair is henselian because $R$ is henselian local. Step 4 says this lift lies in $\mathcal D(R)$. Equality of its generic point with that of a $\mathcal D$-section means equality of the $\mathcal N$-sections (by the injectivity just checked). Hence its reduction lies in $\mathcal D_{\bar k}$.

source.place: Section 3.3 and Proposition 4.3; Stacks Tag 0H74, lemma-lift-smooth-henselian; Tags 01V6 and 02H6

proof.text: The smooth $\bar k$-scheme $\mathcal N_{\bar k}$ has dense $\bar k$-points by [lem-pc-rational-points-dense]. Its identity component is closed, and it is $\mathcal D_{\bar k}$ by Step 3. Step 5 puts every rational point in this closed subset, so density gives $|\mathcal N_{\bar k}|=|\mathcal D_{\bar k}|$. Thus $\mathcal N_{\bar k}$ is connected.

source.place: Proposition 4.3 second paragraph, using rational-point density instead of uniqueness of smooth models

proof.text: The map $q$ of Step 1 is continuous and surjective. If its target were the disjoint union of two nonempty open subsets, their inverse images would be disjoint nonempty opens covering $\mathcal N_{\bar k}$, contradicting Step 6. Therefore $\mathcal G_{\bar k}$ is connected, as required.

source.place: Proposition 4.4(i), connectedness descent along the finite normalization cover

proof_origin.place: Prasad--Yu Proposition 4.4(i), via 3.4, 4.3, 3.5 and 3.7, read online; local copy WANTED. Coordinate boundedness and final section/density argument written out by Q23.
